# Vendored crates

## hayro-jpeg2000 0.4.1, patched

Source: crates.io `hayro-jpeg2000` 0.4.1 (MIT OR Apache-2.0, <https://github.com/LaurenzV/hayro>),
copied unchanged except for the patches below and a trimmed `Cargo.toml` (no `image`
feature, no examples or dev-dependencies; `src/integration.rs` removed with that feature).
`hayro-jpeg2000-0.4.1-shl.patch` is the full source diff against the crates.io release.
Upstream master (commit 9fbc9ef, 2026-10-14, unreleased) still has the bugs behind
patches 1 and 4. It has rewritten the progression iterators (the patch 2 fixture decodes
there without a panic) and adds RGN and POC support, which would replace patch 3. When a
release after 0.4.1 ships, re-vendor it and keep only the patches it still needs.

| # | File | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `src/j2c/codestream.rs` | `MAX_LAYER_COUNT` 32 → 255 | Layers are counted in a `u8` and nothing else depends on the cap. RareCyte slides in IDC use 33 layers and failed with "failed to parse COD marker". |
| 2 | `src/j2c/progression.rs` | LRCP iterator wraps at the largest resolution count over all components and skips components that lack the current resolution, as the RLCP iterator already did | Components may have different decomposition levels (COC). The old code compared against one component's count and then panicked in `ResolutionTile::new`. Found by fuzzing. |
| 3 | `src/j2c/codestream.rs` | Main-header RGN is refused as unsupported (it was skipped) | Region-of-interest scaling is not implemented in 0.4.1, so skipping the marker decoded wrong samples silently. A tile-part RGN was already refused. |
| 4 | `src/reader.rs` | The bit stuffed after an 0xFF byte in a packet header is skipped whatever its value | T.800 B.10.1 says it is 0, but an Aperio encoder in IDC writes a 1. Hayro treated that as an error, and in its lenient mode silently dropped the rest of the tile (max \|diff\| 89 on a lossless frame). OpenJPEG reads only the low 7 bits of that byte, so it ignores the bit too. |
| 5 | `src/j2c/ht/` (new), `src/j2c/segment.rs`, `src/j2c/decode.rs`, `src/j2c/codestream.rs`, `src/j2c/build.rs`, `src/error.rs`, `src/lib.rs` | HTJ2K (ITU-T T.814) decoding, enabled by a new `DecodeSettings::high_throughput` (off by default, so `.90`/`.91` decoding is unchanged): CAP and CPF markers are accepted; code-block style bits 6 and 7 are read; tier-2 follows the T.814 B.2/B.3 pass layout for HT code-blocks (one cleanup segment, which also takes any placeholder passes, and one SigProp + MagRef segment); HT code-blocks are decoded by the block decoder in `src/j2c/ht/` straight into hayro's sub-band coefficients. MIXED tile-components, a second HT set (MULTIHT), HT code-blocks with a style bit other than vertically causal context, and HT blocks that fail to decode give `DecodingError::HtUnsupported`, so the caller (`shl-codec-htj2k`) can use another decoder. | `shl-codec-htj2k` decodes through hayro instead of `oxideav-jpeg2000`, about 10× faster ([htj2k PERF.md](../../../codec-corpus/formats/htj2k/PERF.md)). |
| 5a | `src/j2c/ht/` | The block decoder is `ndic-htj2k` 0.2.5's `src/block/` (MIT, Fideus Labs LLC), a bounds-checked port of OpenJPH's 32-bit block decoder (BSD-2-Clause); `src/j2c/ht/LICENSE` carries both notices. Changes: its error type, scratch buffers reused across code-blocks, the forward reader's common refill (four bytes, nothing to unstuff) inlined, the MagSgn and VLC bit buffers kept in local variables, MagSgn rows written through slices. The encoder is compiled for tests only. | Speed: the block decoder went from 103 to about 80 instructions per sample, and from 37 to about 22 cycles. The round-trip tests in `src/j2c/ht/tests.rs` (1,500 random blocks over every size class and K_max 2–28, plus damaged segments) and the frame-level cross-check against oxideav check it. |
| 6 | `src/math.rs` | `floor_f32` on x86 without SSE4.1 (the default x86-64 target): truncation-based, exact (`f32::floor` is a call to libm's `floorf` there) | 18% of an HTJ2K decode was in `floorf`. A test compares it with `f32::floor` on 1M values. |
| 7 | `src/j2c/idwt.rs` | Each row is interleaved and horizontally filtered in one step, with the lifting done on the row's low-pass and high-pass halves as contiguous arrays (vectorised; the same operations, the same order) | The horizontal 5/3 and 9/7 passes were scalar. |
| 8 | `src/j2c/decode.rs`, `src/math.rs`, `src/lib.rs` | Without MCT, the DC level shift is added while storing a tile, not in a separate pass; a single tile whose IDWT output is exactly the image is moved into the channel buffer instead of copied; `DecodeSettings::defer_level_shift` (raw codestreams only, off by default) leaves the shift to the caller, which `shl-codec-jpeg2000` adds while converting to integers | Fewer passes over the whole frame. |
| 9 | `src/j2c/idwt.rs` | The vertical lifting steps run as one pass down the rows (5/3) or two (9/7, which had five): a row is updated as soon as its neighbours are final | Half the vertical memory traffic. |
| 10 | `src/lib.rs`, `src/j2c/codestream.rs`, `src/j2c/build.rs`, `src/j2c/decode.rs` | Reduced-resolution decoding. (1) A new `DecodeSettings::reduce: Option<u8>` discards exactly that many of the highest resolution levels, as OpenJPEG's `reduce` does: their code-blocks are not decoded and their wavelet synthesis is skipped. A component (main header or tile-part COD/COC) with too few levels gives `FormatError::Unsupported`, where `target_resolution` silently reduced less. (2) Three panics on the reduced path, all found by fuzzing, are fixed, each only when levels are skipped: a tile that is empty at the reduced level (`chunks_exact(0)` in `store`), a tile-part COD with fewer levels than the reduction (subtraction overflow in `build`), and subsampled components indexed from the full-size tile origin instead of the reduced IDWT output's origin. | `shl-codec-jpeg2000::decode_frame_scaled` (CONTRACT.md, "Reduced-resolution decode"). Full-resolution decoding is unchanged: every change is gated on skipped levels. Regression tests are in `../tests/regressions.rs`; results against OpenJPEG are in `codec-corpus/formats/jpeg2000/scaled/check_scaled.py`. The image-offset handling of the reduced path still mixes full-size offsets with reduced coordinates, so the wrapper reduces only images whose origin is (0, 0). |
| 11 | `src/j2c/mct2.rs` (new), `src/j2c/codestream.rs`, `src/j2c/decode.rs`, `src/j2c/tile.rs`, `src/j2c/mod.rs`, `src/jp2/mod.rs`, `src/lib.rs` | JPEG 2000 Part 2 multiple component transformations (ITU-T T.801 Annex J): the main-header CBD, MCT, MCC and MCO marker segments, with Zmct/Zmcc series joined, are read when Rsiz announces the capability; COD's SGcod 2 selects them. After all tiles are decoded, each MCO stage applies its component collections: array-based decorrelation and dependency, reversible (integer, J-4/J-5 and J-15) and irreversible (f32, J-2 and J-12), with offset arrays and null components, in place of the DC level shift. The output is the CBD components; `Image::multi_component_output` reports them. Unsupported: the wavelet-based transformation (J.3.2), any other Part 2 capability in Rsiz, these marker segments in a tile-part header, subsampled components, and Part 2 inside a JP2/JPX file | DICOM 1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.92 and .93. No open-source decoder implements Annex J (OpenJPEG 2.5.4 and Grok refuse SGcod above 1), so the corpus cases are made by `codec-corpus/scripts/sources/j2k_part2.py` and checked against seeds and a numpy implementation ([jpeg2000 FORMAT.md](../../../codec-corpus/formats/jpeg2000/FORMAT.md#jpeg-2000-part-2-multi-component-92-93)). Codestreams without Part 2 decode exactly as before. Unit tests in `src/j2c/mct2.rs`, integration tests in `../tests/part2.rs`. |
| – | `src/lib.rs` | `#![allow(clippy::all)]` | The crate is a workspace member by path; upstream style is not linted against our `clippy -D warnings`. |

Regression tests for patches 1–4 and 10 are in `../tests/regressions.rs`. Patches 1 and 4 are
worth offering upstream; patch 4 also matters for hayro's PDF use.

Patches 6–9 change speed only. Every JPEG 2000 and HTJ2K corpus frame (2,569 and 79) was
decoded before and after each of them, and the outputs are byte-identical. Patch 5 is new
behaviour behind a setting that only `shl-codec-htj2k` sets. Upstream has an open issue
asking for HTJ2K; patch 5 could be offered there, with the ndic and OpenJPH notices.
